name: Demo Plan: Spain 2026
description: 9–16 August 2026: Bilbao, then via Logroño and Tudela to the total solar eclipse in the Bardenas Reales, then Zaragoza and Barcelona.
note: Compiled on 14 November 2026 from the itinerary in the project (as of 9 August 2026). Accommodation locations are approximate (within about 200 m); the other places follow Wikipedia and OpenStreetMap.

places.name: Barcelona–El Prat Airport
places.description:
Josep Tarradellas Airport, the main airport of Catalonia and the second busiest in Spain. It lies about 12 km south-west of the centre of Barcelona. Terminal T1 was designed by Ricardo Bofill and opened in 2009.

On the way out it is only a connection (arrival at 13:15, flight to Bilbao at 16:40); at the end of the trip, the flight home leaves from here.
places.tip: During the connection on 9 August, stay at the airport: the luggage is transferred, and you only need your boarding pass to go to the gate. On 16 August the flight leaves at 17:30. The apartment must be vacated by 11:00; get to the airport by Aerobús along Gran Via or by the R2 Nord train from Sants.

places.name: Bilbao Airport
places.description: The main airport of the Basque Country, in the municipalities of Loiu and Sondika, about 12 km from the centre of Bilbao. The terminal, shaped like a bird with outstretched wings, was designed by Santiago Calatrava. It is one of the few profitable airports in northern Spain.
places.tip: The Bizkaibus A3247 bus takes about 20–25 minutes to the centre. The accommodation expects you between 18:00 and 19:00, so there is no need to rush.

places.name: Basque Suite (accommodation)
places.description: An apartment on the pedestrian Calle de la Cruz in the middle of Bilbao's Casco Viejo, a few steps from Plaza de Unamuno and the cathedral. Two nights, 9 and 10 August.
places.tip: Requested arrival on 9 August between 18:00 and 19:00. The location on the map is approximate (based on the street), so check it before you arrive. The nearest metro station is Casco Viejo.

places.name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
places.description:
A museum of modern and contemporary art on the estuary of the Nervión, opened in 1997. Frank Gehry's titanium-clad building is one of the best-known buildings of the late 20th century, and it started Bilbao's change from an industrial port into a cultural destination.

Jeff Koons's flower dog Puppy stands in front of the entrance, and Louise Bourgeois's giant spider Maman by the river. Inside, among other works, is Richard Serra's installation The Matter of Time.
places.tip: The visit is planned for 14:00. Allow 2–3 hours. From Casco Viejo it is about 20 minutes on foot along the river. The forecast for 10 August says a possible thunderstorm in the morning, clearing in the afternoon.

places.name: Casco Viejo and the Cathedral of Saint James
places.description:
The medieval core of Bilbao, called Siete Calles (Zazpikaleak in Basque) after its seven original parallel streets. It has been protected as a historic ensemble since 1972. It was restored after the flood of 1983 and is now full of pintxos bars.

At its heart stands the Gothic Cathedral of Saint James (Santiago), a stop on the coastal branch of the Way of St James. Right next to it are the arcaded Plaza Nueva and the La Ribera market.
places.tip: The morning of 11 August, before picking up the car. Pintxos are best around noon on Plaza Nueva. The point on the map marks the cathedral.

places.name: Bilbao-Abando station (car pickup)
places.description: Bilbao's main railway station, Abando Indalecio Prieto, formerly the Estación del Norte. Its hall from 1948 has a huge stained-glass window with scenes of Basque life. The car rental offices are here.
places.tip: The car can be picked up from 16:00. In the evening, drive on to Logroño: about 140 km and roughly 1 h 45 min on the AP-68. Logroño should still be around 33 °C in the evening.

places.name: Hotel Ciudad de Logroño
places.description: A three-star hotel at Menéndez Pelayo 7, opposite Gallarza Park, about 700 m from the co-cathedral of Santa María de la Redonda. The tapas bars of Calle Laurel are about 10 minutes' walk away.
places.tip: Check-in from 14:00 until midnight. Parking at the hotel costs extra (roughly €13 a day). The location on the map is approximate, so check it in your navigation app.

commons.subject: Logroño, Santa María de la Redonda

places.name: Hotel Santa Ana Tudela
places.description: A four-star hotel in an 18th-century palace at Calle Rúa 27, in the historic centre of Tudela. The cathedral is about 120 m away, Plaza de los Fueros about 300 m.
places.tip: The agreed arrival time is 15:00–16:00, so check in before leaving for the eclipse (the original itinerary has check-in only afterwards). Parking costs extra, around €15 a night. The old town is a pedestrian zone where navigation apps get lost. The location on the map is approximate.

places.name: Bardenas Reales – Aguilares (eclipse)
places.description:
An official viewing site of the Navarre Eklipse network, at the visitor centre of the Bardenas Reales natural park (Finca de Aguilares). The Bardenas are a semi-desert of badlands covering about 42,000 ha, with buttes carved by erosion, the most famous of which is Castildetierra.

The total solar eclipse on 12 August 2026 should last about 73 seconds here. The site takes 1,000 people and has parking, water, toilets, refreshments and medical services.
places.tip: Turn off the NA-134 (Tudela–Arguedas) at km 15.1, then drive 6 km to the visitor centre. The site opens at 11:00. Tickets and a parking space have been bought in advance. During totality the Sun will be very low above the western horizon, so even a thin band of cloud can get in the way. It should be over 39 °C around 20:00, so bring plenty of water.

places.name: VTZ Hotel Plaza España
places.description: A hotel right on Plaza de España 7, where Paseo de la Independencia begins in the centre of Zaragoza. The Basilica del Pilar and La Seo are a 10-minute walk away, the Roman theatre about 400 m.
places.tip: Check-in from 15:00. The forecast for 13 August is extreme heat (41 °C), so plan sightseeing for the morning and early evening. The location on the map is approximate.

places.name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Pillar
places.description:
A Baroque cathedral-basilica on the bank of the Ebro, built from 1681. It is one of the most important Marian pilgrimage sites and, according to tradition, stands where the Virgin Mary appeared to the Apostle James on a pillar (pilar).

It has eleven domes with coloured tiles and four towers. Some of the frescoes in the domes were painted by the young Francisco Goya.
places.tip: Entry to the basilica is free. A lift (paid) goes up the north-west tower, with a view over the city and the Ebro. The best view of the whole building is from the stone bridge, the Puente de Piedra.

places.name: La Seo Cathedral
places.description:
The Cathedral of the Saviour (La Seo del Salvador) on Plaza de la Seo, Zaragoza's first cathedral. It stands on the site of the Roman forum, a Visigothic church and the main mosque, and mixes Romanesque, Gothic, Mudéjar and Baroque styles.

The Mudéjar wall of the apse, with geometric patterns in brick and ceramics, has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Mudéjar Architecture of Aragon since 2001. Inside is a tapestry museum.
places.tip: Tickets not bought yet. From the Pilar it is about 300 m across Plaza del Pilar.

places.name: Aljafería Palace
places.description:
A fortified palace built in the second half of the 11th century for the Banu Hud, the ruling dynasty of the taifa of Zaragoza. It is one of the most important monuments of Islamic architecture in Europe outside Andalusia. After the conquest of Zaragoza in 1118 it became a seat of the kings of Aragon, and the Catholic Monarchs later rebuilt it.

The oldest part is the Troubadour Tower, named after the play that became Verdi's opera Il trovatore. Today the palace houses the Aragonese parliament.
places.tip: Tickets not bought yet. It is about 15–20 minutes' walk west of the centre. The palace is on the way to Delicias station, so it can be combined with Friday 14 August before returning the car.

places.name: Zaragoza-Delicias station
places.description: A railway and bus station opened in 2003, on the Madrid–Barcelona high-speed line. Its huge hall with a perforated roof was designed by Carlos Ferrater and José María Valero, and the building won the Brunel Award for railway architecture.
places.tip: Return the car (check the return location in the contract) and take the Iryo train at 18:58, arriving at Barcelona-Sants at 20:42. The station is about 15 minutes by car from the centre.

places.name: Barcelona-Sants station
places.description: Barcelona's main railway station, opened in 1975, where the high-speed trains from Madrid, Zaragoza and France arrive. Sants Estació metro station (lines L3 and L5) is right underneath.
places.tip: Arrival at 20:42. The apartment at Gran Via 439 is about 15 minutes on foot, or two stops on metro line L1 from Plaça d'Espanya. Arrival at the apartment is agreed for 21:00–22:00.

places.name: TSA Gran Via (apartment)
places.description: Apartments at Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes 439 in the Eixample, about 500 m from Plaça d'Espanya and the Fira de Barcelona exhibition grounds. Two nights, 14 and 15 August.
places.tip: Agreed arrival 21:00–22:00, with self check-in as described in the email (check it in advance). Check-out on 16 August by 11:00.

places.name: Sagrada Família
places.description:
Gaudí's Basilica of the Holy Family, under construction since 1882 and still unfinished. Gaudí worked on it for over 40 years, until his death in 1926, and is buried in it. The interior is like a stone forest of columns that branch out under the vault, lit through coloured stained glass.

Pope Benedict XVI consecrated the unfinished building as a basilica in 2010. It is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.tip: The €52 tickets are paid for, but the date and time of the visit are missing. Check them on the ticket itself. If they fall on Saturday 15 August, expect holiday crowds. From Gran Via it takes about 25 minutes by metro, lines L1 and L5.

places.name: Barri Gòtic and the cathedral
places.description:
The historic core of old Barcelona between La Rambla and Via Laietana, with remains of the Roman walls and the medieval Jewish quarter, El Call. Much of its “Gothic” look is in fact neo-Gothic, from rebuilding before the exhibition of 1929.

In the middle stands the Gothic Cathedral of the Holy Cross and Saint Eulalia. Its neo-Gothic façade was only completed at the end of the 19th century. Thirteen white geese live in the cloister, one for each year of the martyr Eulalia's life.
places.tip: 15 August is a public holiday in Spain: some shops will be closed and the centre crowded. The cathedral charges admission and asks for covered shoulders. The point on the map marks the cathedral.

places.name: San Sebastián – La Concha beach
places.description:
A seaside resort on the Basque coast, about 100 km east of Bilbao, known for its food and for the most Michelin stars per inhabitant. The crescent-shaped La Concha beach, about 1.35 km long, on the bay of the same name, is one of the most famous city beaches in Europe.

Above the bay rise the hills of Urgull and Igueldo, the latter with a funicular and a view over the whole bay. The old town (Parte Vieja) has dozens of pintxos bars.
places.tip: The itinerary lists it as a possible trip on Monday 10 August, with a question mark, so it is unconfirmed. Buses from Bilbao take about an hour. Watch out for the clash with the Guggenheim at 14:00. On 10 August San Sebastián is cooler (26 °C), with possible light rain in the morning. The point on the map is roughly in the middle of the beach.

places.name: Calle del Laurel
places.description:
A lane about 200 m long in the old town of Logroño, with one bar after another. It is one of the most famous tapas streets in Spain. It appeared after the town walls, which ran along today's Bretón de los Herreros, were pulled down in 1862.

Every bar has its speciality; the best known are grilled mushrooms (“champis”) and pinchos with chorizo, with a glass of Rioja.
places.tip: An idea for the evening of 11 August, after arriving in Logroño. It is about 10 minutes' walk from the hotel. It comes alive from about 20:00, and people usually go from bar to bar.

commons.subject: Logroño, Santa María de la Redonda

places.name: Tudela Cathedral
places.description:
The late Romanesque Cathedral of Saint Mary on Plaza Vieja, built from the end of the 12th century on the site of the main mosque. It was originally a collegiate church and only became a cathedral in the 18th century. It has been a national monument since 1884.

The main west portal, the Puerta del Juicio (Door of the Last Judgement), is decorated with over a hundred groups of sculptures showing scenes of heaven and hell.
places.tip: It is right next to the hotel (about 120 m), so it suits a short visit on 12 August after check-in, or on the morning of 13 August before leaving for Zaragoza.
